paragraphs: Lantus, Semglee and Rezvoglar labels indicate adult and pediatric diabetes mellitus; their pediatric evidence derives from type 1 diabetes ages 6–15 and adult studies. Toujeo explicitly indicates diabetes in adults and children ≥6 years. Basaglar specifically indicates adult/pediatric type 1 diabetes and adult type 2 diabetes; pediatric type 2 use and type 1 use below 6 are not established. Do not assign one universal minimum age to every product.

All selected products are basal insulin and are not recommended for treating diabetic ketoacidosis. In type 1 diabetes, combine with short-/rapid-acting premeal insulin. This profile excludes fixed insulin glargine/lixisenatide combinations and individualized emergency insulin protocols.
These starting regimens require individual assessment; they are not a total insulin prescription.

rows: Approximately one-third of total daily insulin requirements as basal; premeal insulin supplies the remainder.
0.2 units/kg or up to 10 units once daily, followed by supervised titration.
Basal approximately one-third to one-half of total daily insulin. Label rule-of-thumb initial TOTAL insulin: 0.2–0.4 units/kg/day; remainder as mealtime insulin.
Adjust no more often than every 3–4 days. Full glucose-lowering effect may take 5 days; monitor daily at initiation.

paragraphs: Increase glucose checks during changes and early follow-up; other diabetes medicines may also need adjustment.

rows: Toujeo U-300 → Lantus / Basaglar / Semglee / Rezvoglar U-100
Start at 80% of the discontinued U-300 daily unit dose.
Start at the same daily unit dose. A higher eventual Toujeo dose than Lantus may be needed.
Start at 80% of total daily twice-daily NPH or detemir units.
Start at 80% of total daily NPH units.
Same starting units as discontinued once-daily NPH. Basaglar requires individualized intermediate-insulin conversion.
Basaglar label specifies the same unit dose, with supervised monitoring.

paragraphs: Inject once daily at the same time under the skin of abdomen, thigh or upper arm. Rotate sites; avoid pits, thickened skin or amyloid lumps. Use only clear, colorless solution. Do not mix, dilute, use in a pump, or administer intravenously. A pen displays actual units; no concentration calculation is needed. Never withdraw from a pen with a syringe.
facts: 450 units/1.5 mL; 1-unit increments, up to 80 units/injection.
900 units/3 mL; 2-unit increments, up to 160 units/injection; recommended if needing ≥20 units/day. Odd-unit conversion between pens requires clinician-directed ±1 unit.
1-unit increments. Basaglar, Rezvoglar, Lantus SoloStar and Semglee pen instructions limit a single injection to 80 units.

assertion_source_map.card: Renal, hepatic and changing insulin needs

paragraphs: No fixed renal/hepatic adjustment is provided. Monitor more often and individualize units with changes in renal/hepatic function, meals, activity, acute illness or other medicines. Do not apply an arbitrary dose ceiling: device limits describe one injection rather than a maximum daily prescription.

items: Severe hypoglycemia can cause seizure, coma or death. Renal/hepatic impairment, missed meals, activity changes and interacting medicines increase risk; reduced warning symptoms require more frequent checks.
Never share pens, syringes or needles, even with a new needle. Check product and concentration every injection; never use a syringe to extract pen contents.
Changes in brand, concentration, injection site or technique require supervision and extra glucose monitoring. Moving from a repeatedly used abnormal site to healthy skin can cause hypoglycemia.
Insulin moves potassium into cells; monitor potassium in patients at risk. Severe low potassium can cause arrhythmia or paralysis.
Anaphylaxis requires stopping the product and emergency treatment. TZDs with insulin can cause fluid retention or worsen heart failure; review swelling, dyspnea or sudden weight gain.

paragraphs: Do not administer during an episode of hypoglycemia or with hypersensitivity to insulin glargine/the selected product’s ingredients.
The selected U.S. labels have no boxed warning. Severe hypoglycemia, medication errors, anaphylaxis, hypokalemia and infection from sharing devices remain important labeled risks.

Hypoglycemia, weight gain, edema, injection-site reactions, lipodystrophy and localized cutaneous amyloidosis are reported. Immunogenicity occurs; antibody tests and trial adverse-event rates are not directly comparable across products. Excess insulin can cause prolonged/recurrent hypoglycemia and hypokalemia. Treat mild lows with oral carbohydrate if able to swallow; severe symptoms need emergency glucagon or IV glucose and continued observation. Do not give food/drink to an unconscious person.

rows: Other glucose-lowering agents; ACE inhibitors/ARBs, salicylates, fluoxetine, selected antibiotics
Hypoglycemia risk may rise; more glucose checks and an insulin reduction may be needed.
Corticosteroids, atypical antipsychotics, sympathomimetics, thyroid hormones, selected hormones/diuretics
Glucose-lowering effect may decline; monitor and adjust insulin if needed.
Glucose response may increase or decrease; pentamidine can cause lows followed by highs. Monitor closely.
May mask hypoglycemia symptoms; rely on more frequent glucose checks.
Monitor fluid retention/heart failure; consider TZD reduction or discontinuation if heart failure develops.

paragraphs: Published glargine pregnancy studies have not established a clear association with adverse developmental outcomes; observational limitations remain. Poor glycemic control poses maternal/fetal risks, and both low and high glucose require attention. Human milk data are absent or limited; endogenous insulin is in milk. Balance maternal treatment and breastfeeding benefits with potential infant effects and monitor changing insulin needs.

Toujeo is labeled ≥6 years; not established below 6. Basaglar pediatric type 1 evidence is ages 6–15; below 6 and pediatric type 2 are not established. Lantus, Semglee and Rezvoglar have broad pediatric diabetes indication wording supported by type 1 ages 6–15 plus adult studies; their selected labels do not state the same explicit minimum as Toujeo. Pediatric type 1 trial severe hypoglycemia was more frequent than in adult trials; specialist dosing and caregiver training are essential.

Use conservative initiation and increments in older adults, where lows may be harder to recognize. Kidney/hepatic effects on glargine pharmacokinetics have not been directly studied adequately; frequent glucose checks and dose adjustment may be necessary. No eGFR-based fixed unit adjustment is supplied.

Insulin promotes peripheral glucose uptake and suppresses hepatic glucose output. It also inhibits lipolysis/proteolysis and promotes protein synthesis. Glargine’s subcutaneous absorption provides prolonged basal activity.
Time-action profiles vary within and between patients; do not promise a fixed duration for every injection.
facts: Relatively constant concentrations with no pronounced peak versus NPH over 24 hours. Lantus clamp median effect was 24 hours; range included 10.8 to >24 hours.
Onset develops over approximately 6 hours in single-dose clamp studies; steady-state concentrations reached by at least 5 days. Unit-for-unit glucose-lowering effect differs from U-100.
Subcutaneous/circulating active metabolites M1 and M2 have insulin-like activity.
Pen units do not require volume conversion; pharmacologic differences still require product-specific switching and titration.

items: Monitor glucose according to the individualized plan; increase checks during brand/concentration changes, illness, meals/activity changes or impaired low-glucose awareness.
Review hypoglycemia episodes, injection sites, technique, adherence and storage. Check glycemic progress and whether basal/mealtime balance remains appropriate.
Check potassium in at-risk patients; follow weight, edema and heart failure symptoms with TZDs.
Review kidney/hepatic function changes and interacting drugs; reassess dose under medical supervision.
Read the exact device instructions, prime as directed, use a new needle each time and remove it after injection. Confirm product, concentration and prescribed units.
Never share any pen or needle; do not transfer insulin from a pen to a syringe. Use the correct U-100 syringe only for a U-100 vial.
Carry a low-glucose treatment plan and teach caregivers emergency glucagon use. Discuss safe driving and alcohol; lows may recur because this insulin lasts a long time.
Rotate healthy injection sites; keep a clinician-directed plan for missed doses/illness. Do not stop necessary basal insulin or double a dose without guidance.

facts: 3 mL single-patient-use prefilled SoloStar pen · 300 total units

rows: 1.5 mL SoloStar (450 units); 3 mL Max SoloStar (900 units)

paragraphs: Store unopened selected products refrigerated at 2–8°C until labeled expiry; protect from heat/light and do not freeze. Discard if frozen. Follow the exact product/device instructions and write the opening/discard date.

rows: 28 days refrigerated or ≤30°C. Unopened room-temperature storage is also limited to 28 days.
Lantus / Basaglar / Semglee / Rezvoglar U-100 pen
28 days at ≤30°C; do not refrigerate once in use. Room-temperature unopened storage counts toward product limits.
56 days once in use at ≤30°C; do not refrigerate in-use pens. Keep cap on; selected manufacturer table specifies unopened refrigerated storage until expiry.

scope_exclusions: Fixed-ratio insulin glargine/lixisenatide combinations excluded; their indications and doses are separate.
No automatic pharmacy-interchangeability or therapeutic-equivalence designation inferred from biosimilar naming; no FDA interchangeability claim made.
Generic/unbranded products require their exact label/device; no pediatric minimum invented for labels with broad indication wording.

resolved_source_findings.detail: Search surfaced older repackaged Lantus/Toujeo labels with replaced product/storage sections. Current manufacturer records were resolved through official SPL API and used instead.

clinical_review: Every published card reviewed against full relevant primary label sections. Source-reviewed within stated scope; not an independent clinician sign-off.
blueprint: Immutable APAP eight sections, essential safety, three hero facts, cited disclosures, four safety cards and three product cards.
